intro_html: Giouvetsi is what happens when a Greek cook decides the pasta should cook in the meat sauce instead of a separate pot of boiling water. Orzo goes into the pan near the end and swells up on tomato, cinnamon, and nutmeg while the turkey finishes around it. Parmesan on top, straight from oven to containers. Each one carries 725 calories and 62 grams of protein for about $6.04 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $6.04 a container (at everyday cost), and look at what you get for it: 62 grams of protein out of a baked pasta dish. That is a number most protein powders would like to have a word about.
shop_smart: Turkey breast is about two thirds of this batch. Frozen roasts are the cheap form, and the post-holiday markdown is where the real money hides. Buy two, freeze one.
Orzo is just pasta shaped like rice, and the store brand is one of the cheapest boxes in the aisle. Do not let the fancy shape talk you into the imported shelf.
Diced tomatoes are the second biggest line. Buy the case at sale price, because this is a recipe that eats nine cans and never apologizes.
This recipe uses a full cup and a quarter of olive oil, so buy the big bottle. The per-ounce price on a large bottle is usually half what the small one charges.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the turkey breast into chunks and season with salt and pepper. Brown it in the olive oil in a wide oven-safe pot, in batches, then set it aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot until soft, about 8 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, nutmeg, a pinch of sugar, and black pepper for one minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, the tomato sauce, and the beef broth, return the turkey, and bring it to a simmer.
Cover and bake at 350F for 45 minutes, until the turkey is tender and cooked through to 165F and the sauce has reduced.

Stir in the dry orzo along with enough hot water to keep everything loose, since orzo drinks more liquid than you expect. Cover and bake 20 minutes more, stirring once halfway so it does not stick to the bottom.
Uncover, scatter the parmesan over the top, and bake 5 minutes to melt it in.
Let it rest 10 minutes, then move it into your weighed pot and fold gently so the orzo and the turkey are evenly mixed.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is your per-container gram target. Portion it warm, because baked orzo firms up as it cools and gets harder to scoop honestly. Each container lands at 725 calories and 62 grams of protein.

steps: Brown seasoned turkey chunks in olive oil in an oven-safe pot, then set aside.
Cook the onion, add garlic, paprika, nutmeg, sugar, and pepper.
Add diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, and broth, return the turkey, and bake covered at 350F for 45 minutes to 165F.
Stir in the dry orzo with hot water, cover, and bake 20 minutes more, stirring once.
Top with parmesan and bake 5 minutes uncovered.
Rest 10 minutes, then portion by weight into 14 containers.
